definition.description: Metrics calculations (success rate, quality score, averaging) must ONLY exist in metabob-rpc-api. metabob-opencode template-metrics-client must be a thin HTTP client with no calculations.
definition.architecturalBoundary: Metrics aggregation belongs in rpc-api, removing calculation logic from opencode client

currentState.summary: Metrics calculations are split between opencode and rpc-api, creating duplication and architectural violations
violations: template-quality-score.ts performs full quality score calculation locally (0-100 scoring)
Success rate calculations happen in both opencode and rpc-api
Averaging calculations (cost, duration, tokens) happen in both layers

desiredState.summary: All metrics calculations consolidated in rpc-api, opencode becomes thin HTTP client
requirements: template-metrics-client.ts makes HTTP calls ONLY (no calculations)
Success rate calculated ONLY in rpc-api (template_metrics.py)
Quality score calculated ONLY in rpc-api (new quality_score.py service)
Averaging (cost, duration, tokens) ONLY in rpc-api (metrics_aggregator.py)
Single write path through rpc-api endpoints (no dual-write)
Redis writes happen via rpc-api endpoint only

current.description: Dual-write pattern with calculations in both layers
steps: - Path A: MCP tool call to metabob_post_activity_result (JSON files)
- Path B: MetabobCLI.completeActivityExecution() -> activity/complete MCP tool -> Redis
5. OpenCode may also call getTemplateMetrics() to fetch alpha/beta and calculate success_rate locally
6. OpenCode uses template-quality-score.ts to calculate quality scores locally
problems: Two write paths (JSON files + Redis) create consistency risk
Calculations duplicated in opencode and rpc-api
OpenCode clients can compute success_rate locally, bypassing rpc-api
Quality score calculations in wrong layer (opencode instead of rpc-api)

desired.description: Single write path through rpc-api, all calculations server-side
steps: 3. reportExecution() makes single HTTP POST to rpc-api /v2/activities/metrics/record
4. RPC API receives execution data (activity_id, template_id, success, duration, cost, tokens)
5. RPC API writes to Redis via metrics_aggregator.py
6. RPC API calculates success_rate, averages, Thompson parameters via template_metrics.py
7. RPC API calculates quality_score via quality_score.py (new service)
8. RPC API returns success/failure to opencode
9. OpenCode never performs metrics calculations - only displays values from rpc-api
benefits: Single source of truth for metrics (rpc-api only)
OpenCode is thin HTTP client (correct architectural layer)
Easier to test metrics logic (Python unit tests in rpc-api)
Quality score calculations can leverage server-side data (historical trends, comparison)

phase1.title: Create quality score service in rpc-api
tasks: Migrate calculation logic from template-quality-score.ts to Python

phase2.title: Simplify template-metrics-client to HTTP-only
tasks: Remove dual-write from reportExecution() (delete MetabobCLI.completeActivityExecution call)
Replace with single HTTP POST to rpc-api /v2/activities/metrics/record
Update activity.ts to use rpc-api selection endpoint instead of local Thompson Sampling

phase3.title: Remove local calculation files
tasks: Run integration tests to verify metrics still work

functional: Execution metrics are successfully written to Redis via rpc-api
Success rate matches between old calculation (opencode) and new (rpc-api)
Quality scores match between TypeScript and Python implementations
Thompson Sampling selection still works correctly
architectural: template-metrics-client.ts contains NO calculation logic (only HTTP calls)
All success_rate calculations happen in rpc-api (grep shows 0 matches in opencode)
Dual-write pattern is eliminated (single write path through rpc-api)
performance: Metrics reporting completes in <500ms (single HTTP call vs dual-write)
No performance regression in activity execution

riskFactors: Quality score calculation migration requires careful testing (complex scoring logic)
Dual-write removal could cause temporary data inconsistency if not rolled out carefully
Thompson Sampling selection must continue working during migration
